name: Zscaler — Web C2 Beacon (Recurring Uncommon-Domain Callbacks) [host/user-scoped]
xql_query:
dataset = zscaler_nssweblog_raw
| filter act = "Allowed"
| filter ZscalerNSSWeblogURLClass = "Uncategorized"
| filter src != null and suser != null and dhost != null
| comp count() as beacon_count by suser, src, dhost, devicehostname
| filter beacon_count >= 8
| alter user_name = suser, int_host = src, url = dhost, host_name = devicehostname
description: Repeated Allowed web callbacks from one internal host/user to a single Uncategorized (rare, uncommon-reputation) domain — the web-proxy signature of an HTTP C2 beacon. Unlike the broad Correlation-bucket DNS-C2 rule, this rule is deliberately HOST/USER-SCOPED: it carries suser (the exact box user) and the internal client IP as alert entities so XSIAM attributes the alert to the same asset/user the Cortex endpoint alerts are keyed on, letting endpoint + network fold into one case.
alert_name: Zscaler — Web C2 Beacon (Recurring Uncommon-Domain Callbacks)
alert_description:
What fired: >=8 Allowed web requests from one internal host/user to a single Uncategorized domain within the search window — a low-and-slow HTTP C2 beacon to uncommon infrastructure.

Why it matters: a host is beaconing to rare/uncategorized web infrastructure at a regular cadence (classic C2 check-in). Assessed severity: High.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols (TA0011 - Command and Control).

Investigate:
  - Identify the internal client (host_name/int_host) and user (user_name) and the beaconed domain (url); check domain reputation, registration age, and resolution history.
  - Pivot to the endpoint on the same host/user for the process that opened the connection (correlate with Cortex agent alerts on that asset).
  - Confirm the destination is not an expected/authorized service before escalating.
